reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the cited text supports it: Section 17(b) gives Sparkling (Customer) an unconditional at-will termination right on 90 days' written notice, which sits within the fallback's 60–90 day window.
No early-termination fee, penalty or non-refundability charge is present; the only post-termination duties are ceasing use and certifying return/destruction, so no material fallback term fails.

Garman (Vendor) has no convenience right — termination is limited to insolvency and uncured material default under Section 17(c) — so the walk-away trigger (Vendor convenience on short notice) is not engaged.

Shortfalls versus preferred (90 rather than 30 days' notice; silence on pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on a 17(b) exit) are correctly noted in the rationale as minor sub-elements rather than redlined, consistent with the playbook's classification semantics.

The failed deterministic check ('Customer convenience termination present') is a keyword false negative: the clause grants an at-will right without using the phrase 'for convenience'; the rationale expressly addresses this.
Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment was proposed and the rendered text is unchanged.
